body:
Azora has closed its flagship value-add fund, Azora Southern Europe Opportunities III (SEO III), with €1.6 billion in commitments. The vehicle received more than €2.1 billion in interest from institutional investors, reflecting the market’s high level of confidence in Azora’s strategy and in the structural opportunities offered by Spain, Portugal, Italy and Greece. This is complemented by €450 million in co-investment, earmarked for larger transactions and to reduce the concentration of these investments in the main fund, bringing total capital raised to €2.05 billion and investment capacity to approximately €4.5 billion. The main fund is the largest real estate vehicle raised for Southern Europe to date.

The closing includes nearly 30 investors, including some of the largest pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments and family offices from Europe, Asia, North America and the Middle East. The investor base combines a high proportion of investors strengthening their relationship with Azora with the addition of new strategic relationships.

SEO III brings together all of Azora’s value-add real estate strategies across living, hospitality, logistics, offices, urban social infrastructure assets and managed land, together with its digital data centre strategy. Across all of these areas, development and active management are central to value creation.

Unlike models based on generalist teams and outsourcing value creation to external teams, Azora approaches each investment with teams specialised by asset class and in-house development and management capabilities. With more than 600 professionals and integrated operating businesses, the investment manager has a distinctive ability to originate off-market transactions, assess each investment with discipline and maintain full control over value creation through capex investments and management improvements.

At the close of the fund, SEO III had already committed nearly €900 million of capital to various projects, equivalent to 55% of the main fund. This is complemented by more than €350 million in co-investment already committed, representing nearly 80% of the €450 million initially raised for this purpose. In total, SEO III has committed more than 55% of its total investment capacity of €4.5 billion.

As Javier Rodríguez-Heredia, Managing Partner at Azora, notes: “In a challenging fundraising environment such as the current one, it is a great source of satisfaction for Azora to have earned the trust of investors of this quality and with such significant investment volumes. This closing is the result of many years of disciplined investment and building a strong track record. Large international investors have valued this track record and our model based on specialised teams, in-house development and integrated management of operating businesses.”

Cristina García-Peri, Partner responsible for Strategy and Corporate Development, added: “What is most relevant is not only having successfully completed the fundraise, but also having demonstrated our execution capabilities from the very beginning. With nearly €1 billion of capital invested before the end of the year and a significant amount of capital still available, we are in a privileged position to continue taking advantage of the opportunities offered by the market over the coming years.”

Evercore and Clifford Chance advised Azora on the process.

Azora, which operates in the pan-European and US real asset markets, is a leading alternative investment manager with €16.9 billion in assets under management. For more than 20 years, Azora has successfully developed and managed value-add investment strategies based on global megatrends, with a particular focus on operationally intensive assets. To date, Azora has achieved a combined net IRR of 19% on its investments, leveraging its expertise to deliver exceptional long-term value creation and alpha for investors. Azora specialises in real assets and develops value-add strategies supported by specialised, vertically integrated teams by asset class, with in-house development and operational management capabilities.

Azora employs more than 600 professionals across three offices in Europe and the United States. Azora takes pride in its inclusive and entrepreneurial culture and its vision of becoming a force for change in the world through its commitment to the highest standards of environmental and social sustainability.
